summary: Erich Rudolf Jaensch studied philosophy at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD), and Strasbourg (Habilitation). He was an Ordinarius at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and became an ordinary professor at the University of Marburg in 1913.

Linguist Erich Schmidt studied at Graz, Jena, and Strasbourg, where he was taught by Wilhelm Scherer. He held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (1875–1877), the University of Vienna (1880–1885), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1887–1913).
Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, as well as under Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun.

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. During his career, he held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (around 1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (around 1951–1960), and Harvard University (around 1960–1970).

Scholar of Tibetology and linguistics Erik Haarh received his doctorate from the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956–1962) and served at Aarhus University as department head (1969) and theology professor (1983–1993).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University and held an appointment as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University, attested in 2016.
Erik Pema Kunsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications and as a resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Jan Duyvendak, Paul Demiéville, and others. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao (1975–1992).

Historian Erik-Jan Zürcher earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the University of Amsterdam (1993–1997), Leiden University (from 1997), and served as director of the International Institute of Social History (2008–2012).

Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, where he completed his PhD and habilitation. He served as professor of sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.

Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College from around 1880 to 1884. He later held an academic appointment at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania as assistant professor (1950) and professor (1958–1989).

Ernest Francisco Fenollosa, active in philosophy, Japanology, and history/archaeology, studied at Harvard and Boston's Museum of Fine Arts school. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878), Tokyo University of the Arts, and Boston's Museum of Fine Arts (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol and served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine from 1919 to 1922.

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and history, studying under Eugène Burnouf and Etienne Quatremère at the Collège de France. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France, becoming professor in 1861.

Philosopher Ernest Sosa studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He was a professor at Brown University from 1964 and served as Board of Governors Professor at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

Archaeologist and historian Ernst Curtius studied under Welcker, Brandis, Müller, and Boeckh at Bonn, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held professorships at Berlin (1844, 1863, 1867) and Göttingen (1855–1867), later directing the Altes Museum (1872–1896).

Ernst Förstemann was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin and Halle under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He served as librarian at Fürstlich Stolberg-Wernigerödische Bibliothek (1851) and head of Dresden's Saxon State Library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who habilitated at the University of Vienna. He held posts at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems (from 2007).

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he studied under Albrecht Weber. He held appointments at the British Museum from 1866 and became Professor of Sanskrit at University College London in 1875.
